question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x,\,2y,\,2z-x-y⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined in Cartesian coordinates as $z=x-\frac{y}{2}+3$ for $0\le x\le 2$ and $-1\le y\le 1.$ Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S$ with respect to the *downward*-pointing unit normal vector $n.$

*Hint: You're given that the fundamental vector product of $S$ with respect to its canonical parametrization is $||{r}_{x}\times {r}_{y}||=\frac{3}{2}.$*
question.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

Notice that our surface $z=x-\frac{y}{2}+3$ can be written using the dot product as 

$$
⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩\cdot {{⟨-1,\,\frac{1}{2},\,1⟩}_{⏟}}_{-\overset{~}{n}}=3,\,\text{or}\,⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩\cdot {{⟨1,\,-\frac{1}{2},\,-1⟩}_{⏟}}_{\overset{~}{n}}=-3.
$$

Since we require a downward-pointing normal vector to our surface $S,$ we must select one where the $z$-component is negative. This gives us the normal vector

$$
\overset{~}{n}=⟨1,\,-\frac{1}{2},\,-1⟩.
$$

Normalizing this vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =\frac{\overset{~}{n}}{‖\overset{~}{n}‖} \\  & =\frac{⟨1,\,-\frac{1}{2},\,-1⟩}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}⟨1,\,-\frac{1}{2},\,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨2,\,-1,\,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the fact that $z=x-\frac{y}{2}+3$ on $S,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨x,\,2y,\,2z-x-y⟩\cdot \frac{1}{3}⟨2,\,-1,\,-2⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨x,\,2y,\,(2x-y+6)-x-y⟩\cdot ⟨2,\,-1,\,-2⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨x,\,2y,\,x-2y+6⟩\cdot ⟨2,\,-1,\,-2⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(2x-2y-2(x-2y+6)) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(2y-12).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across $S$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}\frac{1}{3}(2y-12)\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{3}(2y-12)\cdot ||{r}_{x}\times {r}_{y}||\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{3}(2y-12)\cdot \frac{3}{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{\cancel{3}}(2y-12)\cdot \frac{\cancel{3}}{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(y-6)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(y-6)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{-1}^{1}(y-6)\,\text{d}y \\  & =[x]_{0}^{2}\cdot {[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-6y]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =2\cdot (-12) \\  & =-24\end{aligned}
$$
